title: Trigonometric Identities and Equations
description: Is (1-cos^2 x)/sin x=sin x an identity? State the exact common domain on which the equality is valid.
outcomes: Distinguish identities from conditional equations and use valid one-sided transformation strategies.
Derive and apply the fundamental trig identities from unit-circle coordinates.
Select factoring, common denominators, conjugates, or sine-cosine conversion to verify identities.
Derive and apply sine, cosine, and tangent sum and difference formulas.
Derive and use double-angle identities, including three equivalent cosine forms.
Derive half-angle and power-reduction identities and select signs using quadrant information.
Convert products and sums of trig functions to alternate forms and interpret signal combinations.
Solve trig equations by converting functions, factoring, and applying fundamental identities.
Use substitution and algebraic solving for equations quadratic in a trig function.
Solve equations involving sin(nx), cos(nx), or tan(nx) and translate solution families back to x.
Write complete periodic solution families and extract all solutions from specified intervals.
Use graphing, bracketing, and numerical methods for trig equations without convenient exact solutions.
